To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a direct, iron‐catalysed method for the amination of aromatic substrates with N‐chloroamine reagents.
iron‐catalysed direct intra‐ and cross‐couplings of N‐chloroamides with aromatic C‐H compounds are possible, and that the reaction can be performed in one pot.
iron‐catalysed amination of C(sp2)‐H bonds with N‐chloroamine reagents is a powerful and versatile tool for the synthesis of amines, tetrahydroquinoline, and benzomorpholine derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and application of functionalized iron complexes for the catalytic activation of C−H bonds.
the development of efficient and environmentally friendly methods for the synthesis of organic compounds.
the development of new catalytic processes for the functionalization of organic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of N‐chloroammonium salts as N‐amino radical precursors is a useful method for the direct C‐H amination of aromatic rings.
the use of N‐chloroammonium salts as aminium radical precursors for direct aromatic amination with iron catalysis is a very promising approach.
this is a useful and reliable method for the preparation of tetrahydroquinoline derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general method for direct amination of C(sp2)−H bonds using N-chloroamines as aminating agents.
N‐chloroamine‐derived aminyl radicals can be used to access a variety of N‐heterocycles, including tetrahydroquinoline and benzomorpholine derivatives.
N‐chloroamine is an excellent reagent for iron catalysed direct C–H amination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iron catalysis is a viable and efficient alternative to the more commonly employed copper‐based systems for direct aromatic amination.
the use of N‐chloroamine reagents is an efficient way to generate aminium radicals for direct aromatic C‐H amination.
the direct amination of C‐H bonds can be achieved with aminium ions as radical precursors.
